title: The selection_tools.py module > Description
text:
Description

MCP selection tools for PyAnsys Geometry-MCP.

Each function decorated with @app.tool() is exposed as an MCP tool.
The ctx parameter provides access to the app context (and thus
to the live product instance and command history).

The query/filter/order/group/extend tools all take an entity_type of
"body", "face", or "edge" and dispatch to the matching typed
selection on the selection builder. Not every criterion applies to every
entity type. The tools report the supported criteria when given a bad
combination.

text:
Module detail



selection_tools.list_entities(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, entity_type: Literal['body', 'component', 'face', 'edge', 'design_curves', 'datum_points', 'datum_planes', 'datum_lines', 'coordinate_systems'], body_id: str | None = None, component_id: str | None = None, name: str | None = None) -> str

List the entities of a given type in the active design.

This is the discovery tool. Use it to find the exact body, component, face, and edge IDs
that other tools expect as input, with body paths and component names for context.
Body and component names need not be unique, so other tools take IDs.

Users refer to bodies by name. To turn a body name into its ID, call this
tool with entity_type="body" and name set to that name. If more than
one body matches, use the component path to tell them apart, or ask the
user which one they mean.

Behavior per entity_type:

"body": id=<body id>  path=<component path>/<body name> for every
body, e.g. id=0:12  path=MainComponent/Cylinder. Pass name to
list only bodies with that name, and component_id to restrict the
listing to one component and its children.

"component": the component hierarchy as an indented tree of
id=<component id>  name=<component name> lines. Component names
need not be unique, so use the ID to refer to a component.

"face": id=<face id>  surface_type=<type> for every face of
body_id. Use it whenever a face ID is needed, or to answer
questions about how many faces a body has or which faces are planes,
cylinders, cones, and so on.

"edge": id=<edge id>  curve_type=<type> for every edge of
body_id. Use it whenever an edge ID is needed, or to answer
questions about how many edges a body has or which edges are lines,
circles, arcs, and so on.

"design_curves", "datum_points", "datum_planes", "datum_lines",
and "coordinate_systems": id=<entity id>  path=<component path>/<name>
for live objects throughout the design, including nested components.
Design curves include construction lines left by modeling operations;
they are separate from body edges. Pass name for an exact case-insensitive
name match or component_id to restrict the listing to a component and
its children. Use these IDs with the PyAnsys Geometry API through
run_python; selection-builder tools accept only bodies, faces, and edges.



selection_tools.create_selection_builder(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context) -> str

Create an empty selection builder in the product backend.

Use a selection builder when a selection request needs multiple query or refinement
steps. Start with select_entities, refine with filter_entities or add related
entities with extend_selection, and use order_entities or group_entities
when ranking or grouping is useful. Save the final set with create_named_selection.
If the requested entities are already known by ID and only need a label, call
create_named_selection directly without a builder. Resolve body names to IDs with
list_entities first.

Call this tool only to start a brand-new selection. If a selection builder already
exists from earlier in this conversation, reuse its handle in the other
selection tools instead of calling it again.



selection_tools.select_entities(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, selection_handle: str, entity_type: EntityType, criteria: Literal['all', 'visible', 'solid', 'surface', 'named_selection', 'name', 'volume', 'surface_area', 'area', 'length', 'x_location', 'y_location', 'z_location', 'color'], name: str | None = None, named_selection: str | None = None, min_value: float | None = None, max_value: float | None = None, color: str | None = None, range_type: Literal['intersect', 'contain'] = 'intersect', body_ids: list[str] | None = None) -> list[str] | str

Query the design for entities matching a property and store them in a selection builder.

Query the design for the starting set of bodies, faces, or edges in a selection
workflow. The result replaces the builder’s current selection for that entity type.
Queries search the whole design. To select only faces or edges of specific bodies,
such as “the circular edges of the plate”, pass those bodies’ IDs as body_ids.
Follow with filter_entities to narrow the set, extend_selection to add
related entities, or create_named_selection to save the final set. Pass one
criteria value with its one or more corresponding arguments. Available criteria depend
on entity_type.

Criteria by entity_type:

"body": all, visible, solid, surface, named_selection,
name, volume, surface_area, x_location, y_location,
z_location, color

"face": all, visible, named_selection, area,
x_location, y_location, z_location, color

"edge": all, visible, named_selection, length,
x_location, y_location, z_location



selection_tools.filter_entities(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, selection_handle: str, entity_type: EntityType, criteria: Literal['volume', 'surface_area', 'area', 'perimeter', 'length', 'face_count', 'edge_count', 'loop_count', 'surface_count', 'curve_count', 'color', 'name', 'containing_surface_type', 'containing_curve_type', 'curve_type', 'is_surface', 'is_solid'], name: str | None = None, find_max: bool | None = None, find_min: bool | None = None, min_value: float | None = None, max_value: float | None = None, surface_type: Literal['plane', 'cylinder', 'cone', 'torus', 'sphere', 'nurbs', 'procedural', 'spline'] | None = None, curve_type: Literal['line', 'circle', 'ellipse', 'nurbs', 'procedural', 'helix', 'spline'] | None = None, color: str | None = None) -> list[str] | str

Narrow the entities already held in a selection builder to those matching a condition.

Unlike select_entities, which queries the whole design, this tool only keeps
a subset of the current selection. It does not search the design for new entities.
Populate the builder with select_entities or another selection operation first.
Use extend_selection when the request is to add related entities. Use
create_named_selection to save the resulting set.

Criteria by entity_type:

"body": volume, surface_area, face_count, edge_count,
loop_count, surface_count, curve_count, color, name,
containing_surface_type, containing_curve_type, is_surface, is_solid

"face": area, perimeter, edge_count, loop_count,
curve_count, color, containing_curve_type

"edge": length, curve_type



selection_tools.order_entities(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, selection_handle: str, entity_type: EntityType, criteria: Literal['volume', 'surface_area', 'area', 'perimeter', 'length', 'face_count', 'edge_count', 'loop_count', 'surface_count', 'curve_count'], curve_type: Literal['line', 'circle', 'ellipse', 'nurbs', 'procedural', 'helix', 'spline'] | None = None) -> list[str] | str

Order the entities in a selection builder by a numeric property (ascending).

This ranks the entities already in the builder. It does not discover, add, or
remove entities. Use filter_entities to narrow the set, extend_selection
to add related entities, or group_entities to partition it by a shared property.

Criteria by entity_type:

"body": volume, surface_area, face_count, edge_count,
loop_count, surface_count, curve_count

"face": area, perimeter, edge_count, loop_count,
curve_count (requires curve_type)

"edge": length



selection_tools.group_entities(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, selection_handle: str, entity_type: EntityType, criteria: Literal['volume', 'surface_area', 'area', 'perimeter', 'face_count', 'edge_count', 'loop_count', 'color', 'name', 'body', 'coincident', 'curve_type']) -> list[list[str]] | str

Group the entities in a selection builder by a shared property.

Each returned group contains entities that are equal in the chosen property.
Grouping applies only to entities already in the builder. It does not search the
design for additional matches. Use filter_entities to narrow the selection or
extend_selection to add related entities.

Criteria by entity_type:

"body": volume, surface_area, face_count, edge_count,
loop_count, color, name

"face": area, perimeter, body (group faces by owning body),
edge_count, loop_count, color, coincident

"edge": curve_type

Backend compatibility: face coincident grouping has been reported as
unimplemented on CoreService CORE_WINDOWS 27.1.0. Do not use that combination
on the affected backend. Other grouping properties, such as area or body,
do not identify coincident faces; use them only when they match the request.
If no supported criterion satisfies the request, report the limitation rather
than substituting a different property.



selection_tools.extend_selection(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, selection_handle: str, entity_type: EntityType, criteria: Literal['volume', 'surface_area', 'area', 'face_count', 'edge_count', 'loop_count', 'color', 'name', 'nearby', 'coincident', 'coaxial', 'connected', 'tangent_chain'], scope: Literal['all', 'visible', 'body'] = 'all', distance: float | None = None) -> list[str] | str

Extend a selection with additional entities related to the ones already selected.

The current selection is kept and matching entities from the specified scope
are added to it.
Use this when a request asks to include entities related to an existing selection.
Use filter_entities instead when it asks to keep only matching entities, and
create_named_selection when it asks to save the final selection under a name.

Criteria by entity_type:

"body": volume, surface_area, face_count,
edge_count, color, name, nearby

"face": area, edge_count, loop_count, color,
coincident, coaxial

"edge": nearby, connected, tangent_chain, coaxial

Backend compatibility: body nearby is unsupported on CoreService backends,
regardless of distance, including zero. Face coincident and edge
nearby/connected have also been reported as unimplemented on CoreService
CORE_WINDOWS 27.1.0. Do not use these combinations on the affected backend
or retry them with different distances. These restrictions take precedence over
the general criterion guidance below. Property-based criteria are not substitutes
for contact, coincidence, or connectivity. If no supported criterion satisfies
the request, report the limitation rather than claiming an equivalent selection.



selection_tools.create_named_selection(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, name: str, selection_handle: str | None = None, entity_types: list[EntityType] | None = None, body_ids: list[str] | None = None, face_ids: list[str] | None = None, edge_ids: list[str] | None = None, beam_ids: list[str] | None = None, design_point_ids: list[str] | None = None, component_ids: list[str] | None = None, vertex_ids: list[str] | None = None, datum_plane_ids: list[str] | None = None, coordinate_system_ids: list[str] | None = None, datum_point_ids: list[str] | None = None) -> str

Create a named selection containing geometry entities.

A named selection is a labelled group of entities that can later be
referenced by name (for example, for meshing or boundary conditions). Use this tool
to save the final result of a selection workflow or call it directly when the
requested entities are already known by ID. Resolve body names to IDs with
list_entities first. It stores the supplied entities. It does not discover
or refine them. At least one of selection_handle or an entity list must be provided.

Typical workflows:

Use list_entities with entity_type="body" or "component" to find body or component
IDs. Then use entity_type="face" or "edge" on a body to obtain the face and edge IDs
to pass here.

Build a selection with create_selection_builder followed by
select_entities/filter_entities/order_entities/group_entities/
extend_selection. Then pass that builder’s selection_handle here to
save its currently selected bodies, faces, and edges as a named selection
(for example, “save the bodies/faces I selected as …”). Use entity_types to
limit which of those types are saved.
The IDs those tools return can also be passed directly as body_ids, face_ids,
or edge_ids.

Extend a selection with additional entities related to the ones already selected.

The current selection is kept and matching entities from the specified scope
are added to it.
Use this when a request asks to include entities related to an existing selection.
Use filter_entities instead when it asks to keep only matching entities, and
create_named_selection when it asks to save the final selection under a name.

Criteria by entity_type:

"body": volume, surface_area, face_count,
edge_count, color, name, nearby

"face": area, edge_count, loop_count, color,
coincident, coaxial

"edge": nearby, connected, tangent_chain, coaxial

Backend compatibility: body nearby is unsupported on CoreService backends,
regardless of distance, including zero. Face coincident and edge
nearby/connected have also been reported as unimplemented on CoreService
CORE_WINDOWS 27.1.0. Do not use these combinations on the affected backend
or retry them with different distances. These restrictions take precedence over
the general criterion guidance below. Property-based criteria are not substitutes
for contact, coincidence, or connectivity. If no supported criterion satisfies
the request, report the limitation rather than claiming an equivalent selection.

title: The selection_tools.py module > Module detail > create_named_selection
text:
selection_tools.create_named_selection(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, name: str, selection_handle: str | None = None, entity_types: list[EntityType] | None = None, body_ids: list[str] | None = None, face_ids: list[str] | None = None, edge_ids: list[str] | None = None, beam_ids: list[str] | None = None, design_point_ids: list[str] | None = None, component_ids: list[str] | None = None, vertex_ids: list[str] | None = None, datum_plane_ids: list[str] | None = None, coordinate_system_ids: list[str] | None = None, datum_point_ids: list[str] | None = None) -> str

Create a named selection containing geometry entities.

A named selection is a labelled group of entities that can later be
referenced by name (for example, for meshing or boundary conditions). Use this tool
to save the final result of a selection workflow or call it directly when the
requested entities are already known by ID. Resolve body names to IDs with
list_entities first. It stores the supplied entities. It does not discover
or refine them. At least one of selection_handle or an entity list must be provided.

Typical workflows:

Use list_entities with entity_type="body" or "component" to find body or component
IDs. Then use entity_type="face" or "edge" on a body to obtain the face and edge IDs
to pass here.

Build a selection with create_selection_builder followed by
select_entities/filter_entities/order_entities/group_entities/
extend_selection. Then pass that builder’s selection_handle here to
save its currently selected bodies, faces, and edges as a named selection
(for example, “save the bodies/faces I selected as …”). Use entity_types to
limit which of those types are saved.
The IDs those tools return can also be passed directly as body_ids, face_ids,
or edge_ids.

Module detail



session_tools.get_session_script(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context) -> str

Get recorded session commands as a reusable PyAnsys Geometry Python script.

The tool returns a formatted Python script containing the recorded backend connection setup
and commands in execution order, not a command list or Markdown. To replay the script,
install PyAnsys Geometry (ansys-geometry-core) and ensure access to the recorded backend
and any referenced files. Replaying repeats the recorded geometry changes.
The script includes only operations stored in command history. It excludes
backend script-file operations



session_tools.get_backend_status(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context) -> str

Get the current status of the product backend.



async session_tools.run_python(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, code: str, timeout: int = 300, no_output_timeout: int = 300) -> str

Perform any geometry/CAD operation that has no dedicated MCP tool.

Run PyAnsys Geometry API code to perform the operation.

This is the general-purpose fallback tool. When the user asks for a modeling,
query, or modification action (such as fillet, chamfer, shell, measure, pattern) and
no other tool matches it, do NOT answer that it is unsupported. Write the
equivalent ansys.geometry.core code and run it here. Choose a dedicated tool
whenever one exists. Use run_iron_python for Discovery/SpaceClaim scripting API
code or an existing script file. Never write a temporary file to run a few statements.

The session is persistent, so variables defined by one call stay available to the
next. instance (the Modeler) and design are predefined. Import anything
else explicitly. Bodies, faces, and edges are reached
through the design tree (design.bodies[0].faces[0].edges) and edits are methods
on those objects. Only stdout is returned, so print() the values you need. Look
up the API with suggest_api and get_api_details before writing the code, and
use the documented signatures and imports as given without re-checking them.
Introspect with dir() or help() only for something the documentation does
not cover, or after a documented call raises an error.

The code runs in a separate process that is connected to the same geometry
service the other tools use, so bodies they created are immediately available
here, and bodies created here are immediately visible to them.
After successful execution, the server-side design cache is synchronized.



session_tools.create_design(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, design_name: str) -> str

Create a new design in the product backend.



session_tools.get_design_info(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context) -> str

Get an inventory of the active design, including objects inside components.

Report counts of components, bodies, named selections, materials, coordinate
systems, datum points, planes and lines, beams, beam profiles, design points,
and design curves (including construction lines created as side effects of
patterns, revolves, and similar operations). Component-owned objects are
counted throughout the hierarchy, not just at the design root. Deleted
components and objects with an is_alive flag set to false are excluded.
Named selections, materials, and beam profiles are design-level collections.

Use this to check what exists in the design, find leftover construction
geometry, and as a final inventory check before exporting or saving.
Use list_entities to discover object IDs and component paths.



session_tools.file_operation(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, operation: Literal['import', 'export'], file_path: str | None = None, file_format: str | None = None, folder: str | None = None, mode: str = 'open', import_names: bool = False, import_curves: bool = False, import_coordinate_systems: bool = False, import_named_selections: bool = True, cleanup_bodies: bool = False) -> str

Import a geometry file or export the active design.

Use operation="import" to open a geometry file as a new design or insert it
into the active design. Supported extensions include scdocx, dsco,
pmdb, step, iges, x_t, xmt_txt, stride, and reader formats
such as CATIA, Creo, NX, JT, SOLIDWORKS, Solid Edge,
Inventor, Rhino, and AutoCAD.

Use operation="export" to save the active design in fmd, step,
iges, scdocx, dsco, parasolid_text, or parasolid_bin format.
Use file_path to specify the exact export filename, or folder to use the
design name as the filename. Do not pass both.



session_tools.run_iron_python(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, file_path: str | None = None, args: dict[str, str] | None = None, script: str | None = None) -> str | dict[str, str]

Run Discovery/SpaceClaim scripting API code on the geometry backend.

Use this tool to execute Discovery/SpaceClaim script text or an existing script
file (for example “run C:/scripts/make_flange.py” or “replay this .scscript”).
Provide exactly one of script and file_path.

When NOT to use this tool: to execute PyAnsys Geometry API code. Use
run_python instead. That tool runs the PyAnsys Geometry API
(instance, design, …) in a persistent session, while this tool runs a
different language surface entirely. To load a CAD/geometry file (.scdocx,
.step, .iges, .x_t, …), use file_operation with operation="import".
Do not write a temporary script file: pass Discovery/SpaceClaim code as script.

Script language

The script must be written against the Discovery/SpaceClaim scripting
API, not the PyAnsys Geometry API. PyAnsys Geometry objects (Modeler, Sketch,
instance, design) are NOT available inside the script, and script variables do not leak
into the run_python session (or vice versa).

Passing arguments

args values must all be strings. The script receives them as a
dictionary of strings named argsDict and is responsible for converting them, for
example radius = MM(int(argsDict["radius"])). Pass {"radius": "1"}, never
{"radius": 1}. Omit args when the script takes no arguments.

Returning values

To get values back, the script must assign a dictionary named
result, for example result = {"numBodies": numBodies}. A script that does not
define result returns an empty dictionary even though it ran successfully.

Side effects

The script might create or modify the active design on the backend. Those
changes are not mirrored into this server’s in-process design state or command
history, so after a script that edits geometry, refresh your view with
get_design_info, list_entities, or visualize before relying on
previously reported names, IDs, or counts.

title: Create a basic heat sink
text:
Create a basic heat sink

This example shows a conversation with a Geometry-MCP assistant: prompt,
tool call with arguments, and result. It creates a rectangular heat sink
and a face named selection for a later thermal simulation.

title: Create a basic heat sink > Prerequisites and conventions
text:
Prerequisites and conventions

Connect your MCP client to a Geometry-MCP server with a running Ansys
Geometry backend. Use a fresh session: creating a design changes the active
design. Python variables persist between calls to run_python.

The calls below use server tool names; clients can display a server prefix.
ctx is injected by MCP and is not a client argument. The Python-style
call in step 2 represents a tool invocation, not a local Python client script.

This is an illustrative transcript, not a captured backend run. Results
describe the expected successful outcome. IDs and selection handles must
come from your own tool responses. No thermal solution is computed here.

The base is centered on the XY plane and extends from Z = 0 to 5 mm.
Five fins run along Y and extend from Z = 5 to 25 mm.
The entire underside, at Z = 0, receives heat from a component beneath it.
It is a single face in this simple model; named selections can contain
multiple faces in more complex models.

title: Create a basic heat sink > 1. Create the design
text:
1. Create the design

Prompt

Create a new design called BasicHeatSink. Make a 60 by 40 mm base,
5 mm thick, with five evenly spaced fins. Each fin should be 2 mm
thick, 40 mm long, and extend 20 mm from the top of the base. Make one solid body.

Tool: create_design

Arguments

Expected response

title: Create a basic heat sink > 2. Build the base and fins
text:
2. Build the base and fins

The same prompt continues with run_python because there is no
dedicated primitive-creation tool. All bare lengths below are in metres.
The fins overlap the base by 1 mm to make the union operation unambiguous;
their exposed height remains 20 mm.

Tool call with arguments

Expected response (successful execution envelope)

The printed message reports completion of the call, not an independent
check of the resulting topology. If execution fails, read error and
stderr before continuing. Do not select faces until modeling is finished:
modeling operations can change face IDs.

title: Create a basic heat sink > 3. Select the heat-input face
text:
3. Select the heat-input face

Prompt

Select only the underside of the base at Z = 0 mm for heat input.
Exclude the vertical side faces and all fin faces.

Tool: create_selection_builder

Arguments

Expected response: an opaque selection handle. In subsequent calls,
replace <selection_handle> with this exact returned string.

Tool: select_entities

Arguments

Expected result: a list containing the underside face ID.
Do not continue with an empty list or a string error response.
An unexpected set of faces needs clarification before saving the selection.

The bounds are in metres: a 0.0001 mm tolerance on either side of Z = 0.
contain requires the face’s entire Z range to lie within this band.
The default intersect could also include vertical faces touching Z = 0.
This query is design-wide, which is appropriate for this fresh, single-body
example; an existing assembly would need additional scoping.

title: Create a basic heat sink > 4. Create the named selection
text:
4. Create the named selection

Prompt

Save those selected faces as HeatInput for scoping a thermal load
in a simulation.

Tool: create_named_selection

Arguments

Expected result: confirmation that the named selection HeatInput
was created. Reusing the same builder saves the faces selected in step 3;
it does not create a new geometric query or rely on a guessed face ID.

This prepares geometry scoping only. In your thermal solver, assign a
material and apply the desired heat flow or heat flux to HeatInput.
Convection, ambient temperature, meshing, and solving are separate steps.

title: Create a basic heat sink > 5. Plot the heat sink (optional)
text:
5. Plot the heat sink (optional)

Prompt

Show a 3D plot of the heat sink.

Tool: visualize

Arguments

Expected response

The plot should show a rectangular base with five parallel fins.
It does not highlight the named selection or display temperature contours.
Interactive rendering requires a display on the MCP server host.
To request an image instead, use {"save": true}; the tool returns
the generated PNG path. Pass that path as image_path to
read_image_in_base64 if your client needs the image data to display it.

Perform a Boolean subtract, union, or intersection on two bodies.

The target body survives the operation and the tool body is consumed.

For subtract, the tool body’s volume is removed from the target.

For unite, the tool is merged into the target.

For intersect, the target is reduced to the volume common to both bodies.

title: The repair_tools.py module > Description
text:
Description

MCP repair tools for PyAnsys Geometry-MCP.

Tools that survey and clean up imported or otherwise defective geometry.

inspect_geometry reports issues without touching the model.

repair_geometry applies one repair operation to a scope of bodies.

Each function decorated with @app.tool() is exposed as an MCP tool.
The ctx parameter provides access to the app context (and thus
to the live product instance and command history).

Module detail



repair_tools.inspect_geometry(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, body_ids: list[str] | None = None, named_selection: str | None = None, selection_handle: str | None = None) -> str

Report geometry issues (defects) found in the design, without modifying it.

This is the read-only diagnosis step for when the defect is not yet known.
Run it to find out what is wrong with an imported or defective geometry. Because it
does not change the model, it is always safe to call. It is also the way
to confirm what a repair actually changed.

If the user has already said what is wrong (“fix the short edges under
0.5 mm”), skip this tool and call repair_geometry directly.

By default every body in the active design is inspected. Narrow the scope
with exactly one of body_ids, named_selection, or
selection_handle.



repair_tools.repair_geometry(ctx: fastmcp.server.Context, operation: RepairOperation, body_ids: list[str] | None = None, named_selection: str | None = None, selection_handle: str | None = None, length: float | None = None, angle: float | None = None, max_distance: float | None = None, allow_multiple_bodies: bool | None = None, maintain_components: bool | None = None, check_for_coincidence: bool | None = None, comprehensive_result: bool = False, distance: float | None = None, area: float | None = None, width: float | None = None, min_height: float | None = None, max_height: float | None = None) -> str

Repair defective geometry by finding and fixing one class of problem area.

Use this to clean up imported or faulty CAD. Remove slivers and small
faces, fill missing faces, merge fragmented edges, simplify over-complex
faces, stitch surfaces into solids, or find and remove logos.

When the user has already named the defect (“fix the short edges under
0.5 mm”, “stitch these surfaces”), call this tool directly. Running
inspect_geometry first is unnecessary. Reach for inspect_geometry
only when the defect is unknown and needs diagnosing first.

operation selects what to repair:

"all"

Run the backend’s blanket repair, letting it inspect and fix everything
it can across the scope. Use it when the user explicitly asks for an
automatic whole-design repair. An undiagnosed problem should go to
inspect_geometry first. Accepts no tuning parameters. If one
is supplied, including comprehensive_result, it is rejected.

"short_edges"

Remove edges shorter than length. Accepts length.

"extra_edges"

Remove redundant edges that do not bound a real feature.

"split_edges"

Merge edges that were needlessly split. Accepts angle and length.

"simplify"

Replace over-complex (spline) faces with analytic ones where possible.

"stitch_faces"

Join adjacent surface bodies into solids. Accepts max_distance,
allow_multiple_bodies, maintain_components, and
check_for_coincidence.

"missing_faces"

Find gaps where faces are missing and fix each detected region.
This can help solidify open surface bodies by closing missing-face gaps.
Accepts angle and distance thresholds.

"small_faces"

Find and fix small face regions. Accepts area and width
thresholds.

"logos"

Find and remove logos. Accepts min_height and max_height.
max_height is required and has no default: if the user has not
given one, ask them for it before calling. Do not choose a value
yourself, because a height that is too large also removes real
features such as bolt heads.
Requires Ansys 25R2 or later (26R1 or later on Linux).
Reports only the backend success flag, not logo or repair counts.

Passing a tuning parameter that the chosen operation does not accept is
rejected rather than silently ignored.

By default every body in the active design is repaired. Narrow the scope
with exactly one of body_ids, named_selection, or
selection_handle.

Partial repair is a normal outcome. The modeling kernel legitimately
declines work that would invalidate adjacent topology, so problem areas can
remain afterwards. The reported found/repaired counts are results
for this call only, not totals for the design. Report them as such rather
than measuring the model to confirm them. If the user asks what state the
design is actually in, re-run inspect_geometry scoped to the bodies
this call modified. Do not count edges or faces by hand.

Parameters

ctx

Context

MCP request context (injected automatically).

operation

str

Which repair to apply. Options are "all", "short_edges", "extra_edges",
"split_edges", "simplify", "stitch_faces",
"missing_faces", "small_faces", and "logos".

body_ids

list of str, default: None

IDs of the bodies to repair. Look up a body named by the user with
list_entities(entity_type="body", name=...).

named_selection

str, default: None

Label of a named selection whose bodies should be repaired.

selection_handle

str, default: None

Handle of a selection builder (from create_selection_builder) whose
selected bodies should be repaired.

length

float, default: None

Maximum edge length in meters for "short_edges" and "split_edges".

angle

float, default: None

Minimum angle between edges in degrees for "split_edges". Minimum
angle between faces in degrees for "missing_faces".

max_distance

float, default: None

Maximum gap between faces to stitch in meters for "stitch_faces".

allow_multiple_bodies

bool, default: None

Whether "stitch_faces" may leave more than one resulting body.

maintain_components

bool, default: None

Whether "stitch_faces" stitches only within each component.

check_for_coincidence

bool, default: None

Whether "stitch_faces" also searches for coincident surfaces.

distance

float, default: None

Minimum distance in meters between faces for "missing_faces".

area

float, default: None

Maximum face area in square meters for "small_faces".

width

float, default: None

Maximum face width in meters for "small_faces".

min_height

float, default: None

Minimum logo height in meters for "logos". Omit to use the backend default.

max_height

float, default: None

Maximum logo height in meters for "logos". Required for "logos". Ask the
user for it if they have not given one. Never guess it.

comprehensive_result

bool, default: False

Whether to fix each problem area individually. This is expensive. It costs one
backend round trip per problem area. Leave it set to False unless the user
asks for it. This parameter is not supported by operation="all",
"missing_faces", "small_faces", or "logos". The face operations fix each
detected region.

refreshes the design itself.

Client setup (Copilot and Gemini)

PyAnsys Geometry-MCP supports two transports for communicating with your MCP

stdio (default): Your MCP client starts the server as a child process and

through a URL.

title: Getting started > Start the server
text:
Start the server

Using the Python interpreter where you installed the package, run this command:

By default, the server listens on http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp. You can change
the address with these options:

--http-host: Host address to bind to. The default is 127.0.0.1.

--http-port: Port number. The default is 8080.

--http-path: URL path. The default is /mcp.

--cors-origins: Comma-separated list of allowed CORS origins. The default
is none.

You can combine these with any other startup options. For example:

Keep the terminal open while you use the server. To stop it, press
Ctrl+C.

The HTTP server does not provide authentication. By default, it binds to
127.0.0.1 so that only your local machine can reach it. If you set
--http-host to an address reachable from other machines, anyone who can
reach that address can call the server’s tools, including tools that run
arbitrary Python code.

title: User guide > What PyAnsys Geometry-MCP does
text:
What PyAnsys Geometry-MCP does

Use PyAnsys Geometry-MCP to access workflows from PyAnsys Geometry
(ansys-geometry-core) through MCP tools. When you connect an MCP-capable assistant, you can ask it to
perform tasks with these tools.

title: User guide > Runtime requirements
text:
Runtime requirements

Meet these requirements:

Use Python 3.12 or later.

Install PyAnsys Geometry-MCP. The package installs PyAnsys Geometry
(ansys-geometry-core) as a dependency.

Make an Ansys Geometry backend available. The supported launch modes are
Docker, the Ansys Geometry Core Service, and Ansys Discovery. You can also
configure the server to connect to an existing backend service. Backend
installation, platform, and licensing requirements depend on the selected
mode.

Tool

Description

List bodies, components, faces, edges, design curves, datum points/planes/lines,

text: Recommended workflows

title: Supported APIs > Diagnose and repair geometry
text:
Diagnose and repair geometry

Use inspect_geometry when the problem is unknown. If you already know the
problem, call repair_geometry directly. Both tools can be scoped to named
bodies, a named selection, or a selection builder.

Use repair_geometry(operation="logos") to find and remove logos. max_height
(in meters) is required and has no default, because a height that is too large
also removes real features such as bolt heads. If it is omitted, the tool changes
nothing and asks the assistant to get a value from the user. min_height is
optional and uses the backend default when omitted. This operation requires Ansys 25R2 or later (26R1 or later on
Linux) and reports only the backend success flag, not logo counts.

title: Supported APIs > Select entities
text:
Select entities

Create a selection builder, add entities with select_entities, and refine
the result with filter_entities. Use order_entities or
group_entities to organize results. Use create_named_selection to save
a reusable selection.

title: Supported APIs > Run other operations
text:
Run other operations

Use a dedicated MCP tool when one matches the requested operation. Otherwise,
use run_python for PyAnsys Geometry operations or run_iron_python
for an existing Discovery or SpaceClaim script.
